absent: Flat image header parsing, version comparison thresholds, flag bit definitions, stack alignment value, and helper routines for header skipping and address translation.
Flat shared library bookkeeping including descriptor layout, count limits, sentinel for unloaded entries, base and break pointer derivation, and memory reservation.
Flat post-load steps including platform initialization hook, argument page preparation, stack transfer, table creation, exec finalization, thread launch, and format registration contents.
Binfmt misc mount and control file handling including registration parsing, delimiter handling, enable and disable transitions, removal ordering, and count limit values.
BPF extension contracts including match predicate, load entry, staged field ownership across chain levels, flag value mapping, and handler lifetime beyond release.
Interpreter file lifecycle including open by path, cloning, write access control, close ordering, credential usage, and quota accounting limits.
Exec context layout including parameter block fields, interpreter path handling, accessibility and preservation flags, argument limits, and stack top defaults.

Synchronization and memory helpers including list traversal and publication ordering, reference counting, reclaim deferral, cleanup scopes, mapping locks, page pinning and release, cache maintenance, and temporary mapping.
User access and data helpers including fault reporting, byte order handling, string measurement, memory comparison and moves, logging prefix expansion, alignment, and barrier ordering.
Error encoding and propagation including error pointer construction and tests, notice versus debug reporting, and exact numeric values for failure codes.

findings.text: Flat executable entry computes stack reservation from argument and environment counts plus string pages on non-MMU, aligns it, loads image and libraries, refreshes each loaded library data area with peer base addresses or unloaded marker, selects flat handler, builds argument tables via MMU or non-MMU path, finalizes exec and starts thread at main entry with recorded stack.

Library data pointer refresh iterates a fixed update window for destinations and a fixed library window for sources, skips unloaded destinations, writes one address cell per library below each destination base, reporting user memory failure.

When GOT-based position independence is enabled the loader skips a header then walks entries until a terminal all-bits-set sentinel, ignoring empty slots and relocating other values through library context, aborting on user access failure or unresolvable relocation.

For newer image revisions each relocation record is fetched from user memory, byte order normalized, its target address resolved then its stored value read; zero values are left untouched to preserve constructor table semantics, other values are conditionally byte swapped when GOT mode is off, relocated via library context, and written back, with access or relocation failures aborting the load.

After relocations the loader flushes the user instruction cache over the code span and clears trailing zero-fill regions covering data tail plus break and stack reserves, reporting failure if clearing faults.
Flat handler initialization registers the flat binary format with the exec dispatcher and reports success.
Handler state bit positions are zero for enabled, one for magic selection, two for BPF selection.

Invocation option flags occupy high bits twenty five through thirty one for disabled, loader, transparent, open file, credentials, open binary, and preserve argv zero; the invocation mask aggregates all except disabled.

Flag descriptor records pair a registration character with a primary option bit, an implied option bit, and a human description; the table binds seven characters to preserve, open binary, credentials implying open binary, open file, transparent implying open binary, loader, and disabled behaviors.
Character lookup scans the flag table linearly and returns the matching descriptor address or a null indicator when absent.

Registration entry combines hash linkage, option and state word, magic offset and length, magic text, optional mask, interpreter path, registration name, control dentry, BPF handler reference plus name, bound interpreter list, active use count, deferred reclaim header, and trailing storage for registration text that other pointers reference.
Registration control write limit is 1920 bytes and delimiter pad allowance is 8.

Matching selects by handler kind: masked comparison over magic window when a mask exists otherwise exact comparison, file suffix after final dot for extension entries, or delegated BPF predicate for BPF entries; only enabled entries are considered.

Handler lookup executes under an SRCU read guard over the entry table, relies on ordered publication before list insertion for safe lockless observation, and attempts to acquire a live use reference, skipping dying entries and returning the first live match or null.

Interpreter binding rejects duplicate names and enforces a maximum count, charges the binder user count quota, allocates one block holding descriptor plus both strings, copies name and path, stores file and quota handles, and publishes via tail insertion safe for lockless readers; lookup finds bindings by exact name comparison.
Binding teardown walks safely, detaches each node, closes its file, releases its user count charge, and frees the descriptor.

Handler release is tolerant of null and error inputs, decrements the use count and only the last release tears down interpreters then defers memory reclaim through SRCU callback so sleeping lockless walkers can finish; deferred reclaim releases BPF handler reference when present before freeing.
Provides release operation for BPF handler references held by registration entries.
Staged per-exec BPF selection cleanup frees interpreter name and optional argument strings, releases staged file reference, clears staged file pointers and accumulated BPF option bits.
Table selection walks from current user namespace toward ancestors using acquire ordering until a populated table is found, falling back to the initial table when none is set.

Interpreter choice first discards any state staged by an earlier chain level, returns the static path for non-BPF entries, otherwise exposes the bound list to the BPF loader, normalizes out-of-range loader errors to exec-format failure, requires a staged interpreter name, cleans staged state on any failure, and otherwise returns the staged name or an error pointer.

Effective invocation options for static entries are the stored flags; for BPF entries staged BPF bits are consumed and cleared to prevent leakage into nested levels, then translated with credentials and transparent each implying open binary.

Interpreter file acquisition prefers an already staged BPF file, else clones the single pre-opened file for entries requesting early open and denies write access, otherwise opens by path at exec time; cloning reuses source path, flags, and credentials.

Argument vector construction for interpreters fails when the binary path is inaccessible, either preserves original first argument or removes it, then pushes binary path, optional staged BPF argument which is consumed to avoid nesting leakage, and interpreter name, updating the argument count for each successful push.
Offers kernel-to-exec-stack string copy that validates length, reserves space backward from current pointer, enforces stack limits, and transfers page fragments with appropriate mapping helpers.

String copy measures including terminator, rejects empty or oversize inputs with fault or too-big errors, moves the stack pointer backward before copying, aborts on stack limit breach, and copies from the end toward the start in page-bounded chunks.

Argument page access has two configurations: one expands and read-locks the target mapping, pins the page from the new address space with write accounting and releases lock and reference afterward with cache maintenance; the other serves pages from a per-exec table allocating zeroed pages on first write and performing no cache or release work.

Length and limit policy differs by configuration: one validates against a global maximum string length and compares the stack pointer against a recorded minimum with cache flush on write; the other validates against remaining stack pointer value, reports no stack overflow, and performs no flush.
Provides removal of the original initial argument from the exec stack, advancing past its terminator and adjusting the count, succeeding immediately when no arguments remain.

Initial argument removal maps each affected page read-only, scans for the terminating zero across page boundaries, advances the stack pointer beyond it, decrements the count, and reports access failure if mapping fails.

Interpreter file close tolerates null and error inputs, restores write access before closing, and is bound to automatic cleanup for file pointers while handler release is similarly bound for entry pointers; interpreter open for registration runs under the control file opener credentials with notice on failure.

User memory and relocation faults during GOT walk, relocation updates, library pointer refresh, zero-fill clearing, and interpreter vector building abort exec with access, format, missing, or too-big errors rather than proceeding with partial state.
Logging prefix for this handler derives from the build module name followed by a separator.
Handler resolution entry establishes SRCU protection then delegates to table walk returning a referenced live entry or null.
